Referee and VAR Confirmed for Celtic’s Premiership Clash With Hearts

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:50
Instaread

David Dickinson has been appointed to referee Celtic’s Premiership meeting with Hearts at Parkhead on Sunday.

Powered By

The official will be assisted by David McGeachie and Ross Macleod, with Colin Steven acting as the fourth official.

Chris Graham will oversee proceedings from the VAR studio.

All the upcoming Celtic fixtures are on our fixtures page.

Dickinson was in charge for a vital game in the run-in for the Hoops last season. He was the man in the middle when Martin O’Neill’s side defeated Hibernian at Easter Road in May.

Get Celtic This MorningThe Celtic news that matters, in your inbox every morning. Free.Sign up free

Daizen Maeda opened the scoring before Jamie McGrath was dismissed following a VAR review for a dangerous challenge on Alistair Johnston.

Dickinson initially showed the Hibernian midfielder a yellow card before upgrading the punishment to red after being advised to review the incident.

Kelechi Iheanacho subsequently scored a late winner to secure a vital three points for Celtic.

Sunday’s encounter will be the first meeting between the sides at Celtic Park since the extraordinary final day of last season.

Hearts arrived in Glasgow top of the Premiership and within touching distance of the trophy, but late goals from Maeda and Callum Osmand completed a 3-1 Celtic victory.

The result allowed O’Neill’s side to leapfrog Hearts and retain their title in the most dramatic circumstances.

Sunday’s game kicks off at 3pm and will be shown live on Sky Sports.

Before Celtic can focus on Hearts, however, they face a formidable European assignment.

The Hoops travel to Lisbon to meet Benfica in the Europa League on Thursday night, with Montenegrin official Nikola Dabanović appointed as referee.

Celtic returned to winning ways against Motherwell at the weekend, but Thursday’s match represents a substantial step up in quality.

O’Neill and his players must concentrate fully on Benfica before turning their attention towards another significant Premiership fixture at Parkhead.
